sentences.text: Tom loved birds.
Every morning, he watched them from his window.
He wanted to help them find a home.
One day, he decided to build a birdhouse.
He thought it would be fun and useful.
Tom had never built anything before, but he was excited to try.
First, Tom gathered his materials.
He needed wood, nails, and paint.
He went to the local hardware store.
The store was bright and busy.
Tom walked down the aisles, looking for what he needed.
He found a nice piece of wood.
It was smooth and strong.
He also bought nails and a small can of blue paint.
Tom was ready to start.
Back at home, Tom looked at his wood.
He had to think about the design.
He wanted a simple birdhouse.
He found a picture in a book.
The birdhouse had a square base and a slanted roof.
Tom drew the design on paper.
He measured the wood with a ruler.
He wanted everything to be perfect.
Next, Tom cut the wood.
He used a saw carefully.
It was hard work, but he was careful.
He cut four pieces for the walls and one for the base.
Then, he cut two pieces for the roof.
After cutting, he had a pile of wood pieces.
They looked good!
Now it was time to build.
Tom took the base and placed the walls around it.
He used nails to hold them together.
He hammered the nails in slowly.
"This is fun!" he thought.
After a few minutes, the walls were up.
The birdhouse was starting to take shape.
Next, Tom added the roof.
He placed the two roof pieces on top.
They made a triangle.
He nailed them down carefully.
The birdhouse was almost finished!
But it needed a door.
Tom wanted to make a small hole for the birds to enter.
He measured the size with a pencil.
Then, he used a drill to make the hole.
It was perfect!
Tom looked at his birdhouse.
It was beautiful, but it needed color.
He opened the blue paint and started to paint.
He painted the walls carefully.
The blue color was bright and cheerful.
Tom smiled as he painted.
He imagined birds living in his birdhouse.
After the paint dried, Tom was excited.
He wanted to place the birdhouse in his garden.
He found a good spot on a tree.
It was high enough for birds but easy to see.
Tom nailed the birdhouse to the tree.
He stepped back to admire his work.
It looked great!
Days passed, and Tom waited for birds.
He watched the birdhouse every day.
One morning, he saw a small bird.
It was a bluebird!
The bluebird flew around the birdhouse.
Tom felt happy.
The bird landed on the roof.
It looked inside.
Tom held his breath.
Would the bird stay?
The bluebird chirped happily.
It flew away and returned with a twig.
Tom smiled.
The bird was building a nest!
He felt proud.
His birdhouse was a success.
He had helped a bird find a home.
Tom continued to watch the bluebird.
He learned about birds and their nests.
He even built another birdhouse for different birds.
Each birdhouse was unique.
Tom loved his new hobby.
He felt connected to nature.
In the end, Tom learned that building a birdhouse was not just about wood and nails.
It was about creating a home for birds.
It was about patience and care.
Tom was happy he took the time to build.
He encouraged others to try too.
Building a birdhouse was easy and fun!
Everyone could help birds find a home.
Tom smiled, knowing he made a difference in the world, one birdhouse at a time.
